title: Natural Occupation Measures for Critical Square-Lattice FK Interfaces
main_claim: For fixed q in [1,4), the rescaled counting measure c(q) n^{-d} sum_j delta_{z_{n,j}} of the critical square-lattice FK Dobrushin interface in the unit square converges jointly with the ordered curve to (chordal SLE_kappa, its d-dimensional Minkowski-content measure), d=1+kappa/8, including total mass, with a single deterministic constant c(q).

issues.location: Sec 2, Inputs 2.1 (trace) and 2.4 (nested plane loops); Lemma two-arm-log (Sec 5); Lemma disk-diagnostic and Thm 1 proof (Secs 7-8)
issues.description: This is inherited, not a new error. The whole argument depends on two results from the companion FKCompanion (Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1<=q<4): chordal trace convergence (label chordal:trace) and nested whole-plane CLE convergence (label loop:plane). They are used for the logarithmic two-arm exponent, the disk-diagnostic limit and the fixed-radius identification. A sibling audit (rank 35) reported a major gap in that companion's holomorphicity step (hol:strict-budget together with gap:closure). The bundled companion source shipped with this paper contains that same labelled step. If the sibling's objection holds, Inputs 2.1 and 2.4 are unproven for 1<q<4 except at q=2, and this paper's theorem is conditional on them. I did not independently re-verify the companion step.
issues.evidence: "This is precisely [FKCompanion, Theorem 'Dobrushin convergence for 1<=q<4', label chordal:trace]"; bundled sources/companions/.../observable.tex:1447 \label{hol:strict-budget}

coverage: I read Secs 1, 2, 5 (all), 7 (all) and 8 (all), plus the statements and key proofs of Sec 4 (Prop spectral, Lemma off-axis, Lemma twisted differences, Prop laplacian). From Sec 3 I read Prop radial, Prop normalization and Cor macroscopic-test, and from Sec 6 Lemma start-probabilities, Prop outward and the start of the reference-band proof. Checks by hand: x=(pi-2lambda)/(2(pi-lambda))=2-d, giving x=1/4 at q=1 and x=1/3 at q=2. x1=-beta(alpha) gives the FK one-arm exponents 5/48 (q=1) and 1/8 (q=2). The identity 2x1+2A*alpha^2=x holds. The stiffness 2A=sigma^2/(2pi)=1/(pi(pi-lambda)) follows from the mixed derivative of the Coulomb formula against the DKLM covariance. The symmetry v(t)=v(-2lambda-t) holds and so does beta(t')=beta(t). The core charge alpha=pi/2-lambda lies in -I_lambda, so the special-charge groups correctly live in D^- (opposite convention). The normalized intertwiner limit -e^{±i lambda} holds, with O(e^{-rho|s|}) off-diagonal terms. The quadratic terms of B(f) cancel, giving O(u^3) on pure bands, and the mixed-band measure bound is u^{2eta0}. The dyadic bookkeeping giving r^{-2-c*} checks out. I checked the exponent arithmetic in the microscopic-amplitude and disk-calibration propositions (relative error versus the lower bound). In Sec 8 I checked the L2 replacement bounds (the separated-pair conditional decomposition Lambda_a q_a, the near-pair sums g^{2-2x}, n^{2x-2} and eps^{2-x}), the boundary-strip sums n^{x-1}+delta^{1-x}, the whole-square content lemma and the final constant c(q)=A0/L. I found no circularity: the two-arm log exponent comes from trace convergence, before the sharp arms that use it. Not fully verified: the complex zero-free and regeneration estimates of Sec 3, the reference-band and exploration construction of the outward coupling in Sec 6, and the twisted-row Laurent and gluing argument in Sec 4.
